name: Maher Ktari
detail: Member of the ARP finance committee; warned against the tax and said article 50 was definitively rejected (10 against, 3 for).

name: Ridha Chkoundali (Chkandali)
detail: Economist and academic; called the tax dangerous and asked deputies to remove it from the 2026 bill (2 November 2025).

name: Abdeljalil El Hani
detail: Chair of the ARP finance committee; announced and explained the committee's dropping of article 50 and relayed its members' view that it would hurt investment. His own position is not stated.

name: Issam Chouchane
detail: Officer of the ARP finance committee; reported the committee's rejection of article 50 and the minister's announcement of a revised text. His own position is not stated.

name: UTICA (Samir Majoul)
detail: Employers' confederation; asked for article 50 to be withdrawn.

name: Business News editorial "La fausse bonne idée de l'impôt sur la fortune en Tunisie"
detail: Opinion piece against the tax (Maya Bouallégui, 24 November 2025).

name: Mohamed Fessi
detail: Chartered accountant who calls the tax "justifiable in principle" but spends the article on the difficulties of the design (professional assets, valuation); not a call for the tax.

name: Mohamed Salah Ayari
detail: Tax adviser who says the wealth tax does not by itself deliver fiscal equity and asks for broader tax base and stricter control instead.

name: Skander Sallemi
detail: Tax adviser who sets conditions (reliable asset data, valuation, administration capacity) and takes no position for the tax.

name: Kaïs Saïed
detail: 24 September 2025 meeting on the 2026 budget: social justice and reduced inequality, no mention of wealth or a wealth tax in the reports found.

name: Impôt sur la fortune immobilière (décret-loi 2022-79, article 23, in force from 2023)
detail: 0.5% on real estate worth 3 million dinars or more: a tax on one asset class (property), the predecessor of the 2026 tax. Not recorded as support; the 2026 extension to movable assets is.
